tagline.text: A beginner-friendly peak near Cebu City, known for its grassy ridge and sunrise camping

location.label: Location
location.text: Between Barangays Cogon and Lanas, Naga City, southwest of Cebu City on Cebu Island

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day to 2 days and 1 night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–800 (per person, transport, entrance fee and guide from Cebu City; excluding gear and meals)

children.text: Mt. Naupa is a peak in Naga City, a short trip southwest of Cebu City, and from the Cogon chapel trailhead it takes roughly 30 minutes to 1 hour on foot to reach its grassy ridge. Known for sunrise, sea of clouds, night views and camping, it suits beginners looking for an easy trek near Cebu.
Mt. Naupa rises between Barangay Cogon and Barangay Lanas in Naga City, in southwestern Cebu Island. The Naga City government's tourism page gives its height as
above sea level and calls it the third-highest point in the city. Other articles list
or
, so the sources differ a little; think of it as roughly
. Do not confuse it with Naga in Bicol in the south of the country: this is the Naga close to Cebu City.
It is popular because it is easy to reach and has great views. It is about
1–1.5 hours
by car from Cebu City, and from the Cogon chapel trailhead to the summit meadow it takes about
30 minutes
for fast hikers and about
1 hour

for most people. The summit area is an open grassy ridge with few trees, so you can see the sea off Naga and Minglanilla, the lights toward Cebu City and layer after layer of ridgelines in one sweep. The city's page describes a 360-degree view, and a 2026 news article compared the grass and hill scenery to a "mini Batanes."

Two routes are known. According to the city page, the Cogon side is a short but steep climb, while the Lanas side follows gentler rolling hills. Most visitors start from the Cogon chapel and pass a farm track, a light wooded stretch, a rocky section and then grassland. There are places to rest on the way, and reportedly a few small stores along the trail selling snacks and drinks. The last stretch is slippery after rain and rocky, so wear shoes with sturdy soles. Trip reports describe farm paths below, then shaded and grassy sections, so the trail is easiest in clear, dry weather.

You can do it without staying overnight, but the mountain is also known as a camping spot. Many people carry tents up to see the sunrise and sunset, the morning sea of clouds, and the night sky with city lights. One report says the campsite near the top is on private land, so check locally how it can be used and where to get water. This guide is not an official facilities notice but a summary that cross-checks the city page and several news and travel articles, so confirm the latest fees and rules when you go. Many trails connect nearby. A 2026 article mentions routes from Naupa to Campo Cuatro, Campo Siete, Calbasaan, Balirong and Matun-og Falls, and Wikiloc has an
11km
day loop through Cogon, Naupa and Balirong. However, signage and trail condition on these links may vary, so first-timers should go with a local or guide.
Near the top the ridge is open, with grass and low trees. On a clear day you can see the coast of Naga and Minglanilla, the direction of Cebu City and overlapping ridgelines all at once.
At dawn a sea of clouds sometimes spreads out with the sunrise, but you cannot count on it every time. Sources recommend a clear, rain-free day and advise preparing for the early-morning cold.
Going up in the late afternoon to watch the sunset and the evening lights is also popular. Be sure to bring a flashlight for the descent.
Many visitors pitch a tent and stay overnight. At night the stars and the city lights below fit in one view, but there are almost no facilities, so plan your own water and waste disposal.
Fast hikers reach the top area in about
30 minutes
and most people in about
1 hour
. The trail is fairly clear, so first-time hikers and families with children find it manageable.
Several articles say village children near the trailhead chapel offer to guide you, with the fee usually quoted at around
. The path is clear, but taking a guide also helps the village.
If you have time, you can add the roughly
11km
Cogon–Naupa–Balirong loop or the route toward Matun-og Falls. First-timers are better off with a local guide.

items.title: Day route
items.subtitle: Sunrise or sunset from Cebu City

children.text: Leave Cebu City. For sunrise you need a pre-dawn start; for sunset, leave in the afternoon.
At the Cogon chapel, settle the entrance fee and guide, check your water and snacks, then start climbing.
Reach the summit meadow, enjoy the 360-degree view and morning light, and take photos.
Head back down the same way. On the descent, walk slowly through the rocky sections so you do not slip.
Come out toward Tungkop and return to Cebu City.
Times are examples. Adjust them to the sunrise time and trail conditions.

items.title: Overnight camping
items.subtitle: Night view, stars and sunrise in one trip

children.text: Start from the Cogon chapel. Climbing with a tent and water usually takes longer, so hurry to arrive before dark.
Pitch your tent at the campsite and watch the sunset.
Have dinner and watch the city lights and stars. Temperatures drop at night, so bring a jacket.
Get up early and wait for the sunrise and the sea of clouds. Some days there are no clouds.
Pack up the tent, take all your trash with you and head down.
The direct flight from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when you book.
From the airport to the Cebu City South Bus Terminal or Tungkop, use a taxi or a ride-hailing app; fares vary with time of day and traffic.

From the Cebu City South Bus Terminal, take a bus toward Carcar and get off at Tungkop in Minglanilla. Motorcycle taxis reportedly wait on the right side of the road near the Sisters of Mary school and Lolo Tinong's Bakeshop.
From Tungkop to the Cogon chapel trailhead, take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal). One article gave about
from Rikio Highway to the Cogon chapel and about
for the bus leg, but fares change, so ask before you ride.
Tell the driver "Mt. Naupa trailhead." Some reports mention that the last stretch includes a rough road.
A 2026 article says to head from Cebu City along the southern road toward Naga, turn right at Tungkop in Minglanilla and follow the signs to the Cogon chapel. It takes about
1–1.5 hours
depending on traffic.
Parking is said to be available near the chapel, and it is easiest to set the Cogon chapel as your destination in a map app.

December to May, the dry season, is the best time to walk and the most likely time to get stars and sunrise. In the rainy season the trail is muddy and slippery, and locals advise avoiding the heavy rainy season.
The best times of day are around sunrise and sunset; at midday the grassy ridge has little shade and gets very hot.
A 2013 trip report describes the climb as passing a farm track, a light wood, a rocky clearing and a rest stop with a single house, then about
15 minutes
of grassland at the end. First light arrives about
15 minutes
before sunrise, so for sunrise photos it is better to be in position before the sun comes up.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Best for sunrise and stargazing. Mornings are chilly.
Climb at dawn or in the late afternoon and carry plenty of water.
The trail is slippery, and clouds can block the view.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.

There is no lodging on the mountain and camping is the main option. If you are not staying overnight, it is easier to stay in Cebu City, Minglanilla or Naga town and travel early in the morning. Around Tungkop, where the Sisters of Mary school and Lolo Tinong's Bakeshop are, you can reportedly buy simple bread and drinks.

There are no restaurants on the mountain. Bring your own water, snacks and packed meals. One article mentions small stores along the trail selling snacks and drinks, but whether they are open is not guaranteed. Always carry your trash down.

If you camp, packing light matters. Basics are a tent, sleeping bag, mat, headlamp, warm layers and spare water, and many people manage with ready-to-eat food instead of a gas stove. The summit is an open meadow exposed to wind, so stake the tent lines firmly and pick a spot with a clear view of the city lights and stars at night, keeping some distance from other campers.
If you aim for sunrise or sunset, the walk is about
30 minutes–1 hour
, but bring a flashlight (headlamp) in case it gets dark.
Bring plenty of water; if camping, check beforehand whether to carry it up or get it locally. One report says the fee for hauling water up to the campsite was negotiated separately.
Wear sneakers or trekking shoes with grip. The rocky sections are hard on the soles of your feet.
When passing through the village, greet residents or guides near the chapel and take their directions. Giving a young guide around
is described as the custom.
One article mentions village dogs at the campsite nicknamed "guardian dogs." Do not leave food unattended.
It gets cold at dawn and at night, so bring a thin windbreaker or jacket.
Signage and conditions on the connecting trails (Balirong, Matun-og Falls and others) vary, so first-timers should go with a local guide.
Fees and rules can change, so check the latest announcements with the city tourism office (the official Naga City Facebook page) or village contacts in Cogon.
The summit grass has almost no shade, so if you climb during the day, protect yourself from the sun with a hat, sunscreen and a thin long-sleeved shirt.
Do not climb in the rainy season or after rain, when the rocky trail and grass are slippery, and camp only on clear days.
The height of Mt. Naupa differs by source, from 550 to 590 m, and this guide uses the city's figure of 584 m. The entrance fee also varies (₱20–25), so confirm when you go.
One report says the campsite near the top is on private land, so ask locally how it may be used and what it costs before camping.
Contacts, fees and road conditions can change. Leave plenty of time so you do not come down after dark.
You will ride a motorcycle taxi, so check whether a helmet is provided and agree on the fare before you get on. The last stretch includes a rough road.
There are no trash bins on the mountain, so take everything you bring back down with you.
It is about
1–1.5 hours
by car. After a sunrise on the mountain, come back to the city and visit the Basilica del Santo Niño or Magellan's Cross to make a full day.
A viewpoint on a hill north of Cebu City, a city-style lookout comparable to Mt. Naupa if you want a night view.
A town on the road running south, and the bus toward Naupa is often marked Carcar. It pairs well with a southern itinerary.
Naga's town center, with the plaza, boardwalk and church, lies in the same city. It is easy to stop by after the descent.
